text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user pairwise BPR, sampling one positive and one negative impression per eligible training user while retaining the factorization-machine architecture, request-context features, split, and evaluation protocol.
rationale: The official model ranks within users, so pairwise optimization directly targets the ordering objective. The current model has a sizable gap between global AUC and GAUC, suggesting row-level BCE optimization may not fully align with within-user ranking.
exact_ablation: Ablate pointwise BCE training and replace it with one sampled within-user BPR positive-negative pair per eligible user; change no features, architecture, split, or evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of 0.003 to 0.010 from better positive-versus-negative ordering; estimated validation GAUC 0.672 to 0.679.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of 0.002 to 0.008, especially for users with two to four positives where current nDCG@5 is 0.7698 but ranking quality remains sensitive to ordering.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with a within-user listwise softmax loss over each user's impressions, using bounded user groups or sampled groups to keep computation finite and retaining the factorization-machine scorer and request-context features.
rationale: A listwise objective can optimize relative probability mass across each user's candidate set more directly than BCE and may improve top-five concentration, which is currently weaker than row-level discrimination.
exact_ablation: Ablate pointwise BCE and train with a user-group listwise softmax loss using the same features, FM architecture, split, and evaluation protocol.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of 0.002 to 0.009, with uncertainty from variable group sizes; estimated GAUC 0.671 to 0.678.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of 0.004 to 0.012 because listwise gradients emphasize the highest-ranked relevant impressions; the largest opportunity is the tab 8 slice with nDCG@5 0.0263.

text: Reduce the FM interaction embedding dimension from 16 to 8 while preserving the same five impression-time categorical fields, pointwise BCE loss, optimizer, and stopping rule.
rationale: The context-augmented FM improved official GAUC from 0.6499 to 0.6689, but the larger embedding may overfit sparse user-context combinations. A smaller interaction space is a controlled capacity ablation that may improve generalization and runtime.
exact_ablation: Ablate half of the FM interaction capacity by changing only the embedding dimension from 16 to 8; retain features, loss, learning rate, split, and evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected neutral to slightly positive change of -0.001 to +0.003; estimated GAUC 0.668 to 0.672 if sparse interactions are overfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected neutral to slightly positive change of -0.001 to +0.004; top-five quality may benefit from less noisy context interactions.

text: Remove FM interaction terms and retain only additive field weights for user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, and weekday, keeping pointwise BCE training and all data handling unchanged.
rationale: This isolates whether the observed gain comes from cross-field interactions or simply from additive request-context effects. It is a useful negative-control ablation and tests whether FM complexity is necessary.
exact_ablation: Ablate the FM pairwise interaction term only, replacing the scorer with the additive sum of its existing field weights; retain the same encoded fields, BCE loss, optimizer, split, and evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected decrease of 0.006 to 0.020 because experiment 2's FM architecture likely captures user-item-context compatibility; estimated GAUC 0.649 to 0.663.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected decrease of 0.004 to 0.015, with potentially larger losses in context-sensitive slices such as tab 8.

text: Remove weekday from the request-context feature group while retaining tab and hourmin in the factorization-machine scorer, with pointwise BCE training and the same protocol.
rationale: The screening evidence supports request context overall, but weekday may add less fine-grained signal than tab and time-of-day. This field-level ablation tests whether the feature group can be simplified without sacrificing ranking quality.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the weekday field from the existing request-context inputs; keep tab, hourmin, IDs, FM architecture, BCE training, split, and evaluator fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small decrease of 0.0005 to 0.003 because weekday is part of the measured context lift but likely less informative than tab and hourmin; estimated GAUC 0.666 to 0.6684.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected small decrease of 0.0005 to 0.003, with the possibility of no change if weekday mainly affects calibration rather than within-user ordering.

text: Remove hourmin from the request-context feature group while retaining tab and weekday in the factorization-machine scorer, keeping all training and evaluation choices fixed.
rationale: Hour-level slices vary substantially, including weak results at hours 3, 4, and 8, so hourmin may be noisy at the current granularity. Removing it tests whether the overall request-context gain is robust to eliminating a potentially overfit field.
exact_ablation: Ablate only hourmin from the encoded inputs; retain tab, weekday, user_id, video_id, FM interactions, BCE loss, split, and evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected change from -0.003 to +0.001 because hourmin has heterogeneous slice performance and may overfit sparse time buckets; estimated GAUC 0.666 to 0.670.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected change from -0.003 to +0.002; removing noisy hour interactions could modestly improve top-five stability but may hurt time-dependent ranking.

text: Remove tab from the request-context feature group while retaining hourmin and weekday in the factorization-machine scorer, with unchanged pointwise BCE training and evaluation.
rationale: Tab 8 is the weakest diagnostic slice, and several tabs have extremely low nDCG@5, indicating that tab-specific embeddings may be brittle. This ablation tests whether tab helps overall or mainly introduces sparse context overfitting.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the tab field; retain hourmin, weekday, IDs, FM interactions, BCE loss, split, and evaluator unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected decrease of 0.001 to 0.006 because tab contributed to the positive request-context screening lift, despite poor sparse slices; estimated GAUC 0.663 to 0.668.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected change from -0.004 to +0.002; removing tab embeddings may improve brittle low-support contexts but could reduce useful exposure-mode separation.

text: Replace uniform random mini-batch sampling with user-balanced mini-batches that cap each user's contribution per batch, retaining pointwise BCE, the FM scorer, request-context fields, and the same number of epochs.
rationale: The official GAUC weights users through positive counts, while ordinary row batches can be dominated by high-volume users. User-balanced batches may improve representation for sparse users and top-five behavior without changing inference features.
exact_ablation: Ablate uniform row sampling and use user-balanced mini-batches with at most a fixed number of rows per user; keep model, BCE loss, feature set, split, and evaluator fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of 0.001 to 0.006 by reducing dominance from prolific users; estimated GAUC 0.670 to 0.675.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of 0.002 to 0.007, particularly for users with two to four positives where current nDCG@5 is 0.7698 but training representation may be uneven.

text: Replace uniform negative weighting in BCE with a fixed positive-class weight of 1.5, leaving the FM architecture, features, optimizer, mini-batching, split, and ranking evaluator unchanged.
rationale: The validation long-view prevalence is 0.313, and top-five retrieval remains imperfect despite strong row-level discrimination. Modest positive weighting may prioritize recall of relevant impressions and improve top-five ranking without introducing unavailable data.
exact_ablation: Ablate unweighted BCE and use only a fixed 1.5 positive-class BCE weight; make no other loss, feature, architecture, or sampling change.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of 0.000 to 0.004, with possible neutral impact because weighting changes score emphasis rather than pairwise ordering; estimated GAUC 0.669 to 0.673.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of 0.001 to 0.006 by moving relevant impressions upward, especially for users with only one positive where current nDCG@5 is 0.7987 but retrieval is sensitive to rank.

text: Increase FM L2 regularization from 1e-6 to 1e-4 while retaining the existing five-field input, 16-dimensional interactions, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and stopping rule.
rationale: The model combines high-cardinality IDs with sparse request-context categories, creating overfitting risk. Stronger regularization is a low-runtime generalization ablation that may stabilize weak context and rare-item slices.
exact_ablation: Ablate the existing 1e-6 L2 setting and use only 1e-4 L2 regularization; retain architecture, features, BCE, optimizer, split, and evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected change from -0.002 to +0.004; rare-item GAUC is only 0.6000 and stronger regularization may improve generalization, giving estimated overall GAUC 0.667 to 0.673.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected change from -0.002 to +0.005; smoothing sparse embeddings may improve the tab 8 nDCG@5 of 0.0263, though excessive shrinkage could reduce personalization.

text: Replace validation-proxy GAUC early stopping with validation-proxy nDCG@5 early stopping, preserving the same FM model, pointwise BCE, features, optimizer, epoch budget, and official final evaluator.
rationale: The current stopping proxy optimizes within-user AUC while the official objective equally includes nDCG@5. Selecting checkpoints by a training-only nDCG@5 proxy may better preserve top-five quality, which is currently the weaker metric relative to row-level discrimination.
exact_ablation: Ablate validation-proxy GAUC checkpoint selection and select the best checkpoint using a training-only nDCG@5 proxy; do not use labels from the official validation evaluator for feature or hyperparameter fitting beyond the existing protocol.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected change from -0.002 to +0.004 because checkpoint selection may trade a small amount of AUC for better list quality; estimated GAUC 0.667 to 0.672.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of 0.002 to 0.010 by directly preserving top-five ordering, with the largest potential benefit in weak contexts such as tab 8.

text: Replace one-pass random training order with deterministic chronological training order within the existing training split, while keeping the FM architecture, request-context features, pointwise BCE, learning rate, and stopping rule unchanged.
rationale: The request-context screening lift is positive on every internal holdout date but varies from 0.00067 to 0.00913, indicating temporal drift. Chronological training may reduce instability from random order and better match the temporal validation boundary without adding any unavailable feature.
exact_ablation: Ablate random permutation of training rows and process rows in chronological order with deterministic within-day ordering; change no features, model, loss, split, or evaluator.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected change from -0.003 to +0.003; temporal ordering may improve drift alignment but can also reduce stochastic mixing, giving estimated GAUC 0.666 to 0.672.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected change from -0.003 to +0.004, with potential gains if recent context patterns transfer to validation; estimated nDCG@5 0.534 to 0.541.
